title: Pre-Transformer Generation
motto: If a word is surprising, the model is bad. Perplexity makes surprise a number. Smoothing keeps it finite.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: If a word is surprising, the model is bad. Perplexity makes surprise a number. Smoothing keeps it finite.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Before transformers, before RNNs, before word embeddings, a language model predicted the next word by counting how often it followed the previous `n-1` words. Count "the cat" → "sat" 47 times, "the cat" → "jumped" 12 times, "the cat" → "refrigerator" 0 times. Normalize to get a probability distribution.

That is an n-gram language model. It ran every speech recognizer, every spell checker, and every phrase-based machine translation system from 1980 through 2015. It still runs when you need cheap on-device language modeling.
